Do You Want to Build a...
Cultural Phenomenon?
subhed: The evolution of the Frozen franchise in Japan

intro.text: Once upon a time, in a world swept away by magic and melody, Frozen captured hearts everywhere with its timeless tale of love, courage and self-acceptance. With unforgettable songs, beloved characters and a warmth that resonated across generations, Frozen didn’t just tick the boxes of a Disney classic; it became a worldwide sensation.

In Japan, Frozen was having a cultural moment of its own. Embraced by children and adults alike, the soaring ballad “Let It Go” (ありのままで, or ari no mama de in Japanese) echoed through classrooms, living rooms and concert halls. The franchise's remarkable success was no coincidence; it was the beautiful result of a powerful story brought to life with every facet of The Walt Disney Company — from studio production to merchandise and theme park experiences — working in harmony.

transition: So, let us pull back the curtain and discover the magic behind the momentum.

text: The original Frozen film debuted in November 2013, and quickly became an Oscar®-winning, US$1.29 billion blockbuster. Although fans in Japan had to wait until March 2014 to experience the wonder, the film shattered box office records within just two months of its theatrical release, surpassing 20 billion yen and setting a new milestone for Walt Disney Studios Japan.

Two charming animated shorts – Frozen Fever (2015) and Olaf’s Frozen Adventure (2018) – kept the excitement alive as fans eagerly awaited Frozen II’s arrival in 2019. In 2023, for Disney’s 100th anniversary, the 2D dubbed version of Frozen was shown in 100 cinemas worldwide, inviting families to relive the magic alongside other iconic Disney films.

outro.text: Today, Frozen continues to inspire fans across generations. As the countdown to Frozen 3 begins, the enchanting world of Arendelle is poised to reveal even more frosty adventures and heartwarming moments that will captivate our hearts and spark imagination once again.
